subject.title: Plugin-state entries() can materialize over 3 GiB of JSON in one call

question: What permanent compatibility behavior should the shipped Plugin SDK `entries()` method have after bounded pagination is introduced?
rationale: The availability boundary is source-proven, but the existing complete-array method is shipped public API, so automation cannot choose its deprecation, rejection, or versioning policy.

options.title: Add pagination and deprecate
options.body: Add a bounded page API, migrate bundled callers, and temporarily retain `entries()` with explicit deprecation and oversized-read guidance.

options.title: Reject oversized reads
options.body: Preserve complete-array semantics only below an aggregate threshold and return a typed limit error for larger namespaces.

options.title: Version the contract
options.body: Introduce bounded enumeration only through a new versioned SDK contract and leave the current method unchanged.

recommendation.title: Add pagination and deprecate
recommendation.body: Add a bounded page API, migrate bundled callers, and temporarily retain `entries()` with explicit deprecation and oversized-read guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows the broadest ownership across the public plugin-state contract, storage migrations, and central caller paths.
